messages:
hao: heads-up — saw consistent reranker score drift after HF->Redwood conversion for bert-reranker-1.1. small but reproducible.
liz: ah — how big is the drift and on which evals? :thinking_face:
hao: ~3-5% MRR drop on our QA rerank set (n=10). embedding cos-sim means changed by ~0.03 on avg. not huge but consistent across seeds.
devendra: any change in tokenization or pooling config during conversion?
hao: yes that's the suspicion. HF config had \"cls_token_at_end\": false, truncation=\"longest_first\". our conversion script didn't copy cls_token_at_end and we defaulted to CLS at end. also Redwood runtime applies an internal truncation \"only_first\" for pair inputs unless you set \"pair_truncation\".
jamal: that explains it. reranker expects CLS at start for pooling (we use CLS pooling with index 0). moving CLS shifts positional encodings for all tokens -> different pooled vector.
liz: can you paste the exact snippets? maybe conversion bug in map_special_tokens.
hao: pasted below (from conversion log):
```
# hf_to_rw.py --model bert-reranker-1.1 --out /tmp/rw/bert-rr
loaded config.json
source config: {\"cls_token_id\": 101, \"cls_token_at_end\": false, \"pad_token_id\": 0, \"truncation_strategy\": \"longest_first\"}
writing rw_config.json (missing cls_token_at_end -> default true)
```
liz: yikes — defaulting to true means CLS moved to tail. that will break our CLS pooling.
devendra: for quick triage, can we run two converts: one forcing cls_token_at_end=false and another leaving default, then compare token ids and pooled embeddings?
hao: done. quick results:
- forced cls_at_end=false -> pooled vec stable vs HF baseline, MRR drop 0.5%
- default convert -> pooled vec shifted, MRR drop 4.2%
sample tokens (first 8 ids):
HF baseline: [101, 2023, 2003, 1037, ...]
default converted: [2023, 2003, 1037, ..., 101]
jamal: also check truncation: HF longest_first will remove tokens from both sides; Redwood only_first will chop the second sequence. For pair inputs (query|doc) that asymmetry can change which tokens survive.
liz: right — our reranker concatenates [CLS] query [SEP] doc [SEP]. If doc gets chopped differently, doc-level info shifts.
devendra: fix plan:
1) ensure conversion copies cls_token_at_end and pad_token_id exactly
2) add explicit \"pair_truncation\": \"longest_first\" in rw_config
3) add unit tests: tokenization roundtrip + pooled embedding closeness threshold
4) update hf_to_rw.py to warn when defaults diverge
hao: implemented patch  — added explicit fields and a warning. also added a small regression test in CI that runs a 256-token synthetic pair and checks MRR diff < 1%.
liz: any interaction with quantization? we recently tried int8 for this model and saw tiny extra drift.
devendra: quantization affects activations and can amplify small tokenization differences. but main root cause here is token mapping + truncation.
jamal: for reranker pooling we should also support a \"pooling_spec\" mapping in rw_config, e.g. \"pooling\": \\{\"type\": \"cls\", \"position\": \"start\"\\} so conversion can't silently change semantics.
hao: added a minimal pooling_spec and attached to patch.

token-bot: deploy-bot: conversion-patch-1837654321 merged to staging, CI passed (tokenization unit test). :rocket:

liz: awesome. next steps — run the signing eval suite on staging (full QA+web rerank) and re-run the quantized experiments to confirm combined effects.
hao: will run overnight and report back tomorrow.
